# sngl:async's Lifetime on every target: a request handed one that has ended
# answers `cancelled` without asking, and ending one stops a request in
# flight, which then answers `cancelled` at once rather than when the server
# would have (`/status/200?after=3000`). The second half is the pattern
# async.query is -- a lifetime per mount, ended by the unmount -- so moving
# an effect to another key stops the request for the old one.
#
# The interpreter makes a request where it is called and waits for it there,
# so it has none in flight to stop; it runs the first half only. The second
# ends each lifetime from the program, since android's test waits for the
# program's requests after each step.

sngl test --platform=none ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html inflight.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go inflight.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go inflight.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go inflight.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin ended.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin inflight.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- ended.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import http "sngl:http"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func kindOf(r async.Result[http.Response]) string {
    match var got = r {
        failed { return "{got.kind}" }
        ok { return "ok" }
    }
}

component ended ui.node {
    var kind = ""
    var before = false
    ui.button #ask(text="ask", @click {
        var life = async.begin()
        life.end()
        before = life.ended()
        kind = kindOf(http.get(url="http://127.0.0.1:47819/status/200", life=life))
    })
}

// A request handed a lifetime already ended answers `cancelled` without
// asking, and `forever` never ends.
func testAnEndedLifetimeAsksNothing(t test.Test, c ended) {
    c.ask.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.kind != "", 1500)
    t.assert(c.before && c.kind == "cancelled" && !async.forever.ended())
}

ui.window {
    ended()
}
-- inflight.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import http "sngl:http"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// Answers after `ms`, under `life`.
func slow(ms int, life async.Lifetime) => http.get(url="http://127.0.0.1:47819/status/200?after={ms}", life=life)

func kindOf(r async.Result[http.Response]) string {
    match var got = r {
        failed { return "{got.kind}" }
        ok { return "ok" }
    }
}

// One request outlives the other by seconds, and the short one's answer ends
// the long one's lifetime: everything happens while the program runs, since
// a test step may wait for the program's requests to finish.
component manual ui.node {
    var life = async.forever
    var kind = ""
    effect(@mount {
        life = async.begin()
        kind = kindOf(slow(3000, life))
    })
    effect(@mount {
        var r = slow(100, async.forever)
        life.end()
    })
}

// Ending a lifetime stops the request handed it, which answers `cancelled`
// at once rather than when the server would have.
func testEndingALifetimeCancelsItsRequest(t test.Test, c manual) {
    t.wait(func() => c.kind != "", 1500)
    t.assert(c.kind == "cancelled")
}

component keyed ui.node {
    var key = "a"
    var life = async.forever
    var kinds list[string] = []
    effect(
        on = key,
        @mount(k) {
            life = async.begin()
            var r = slow(k == "a" ? 3000 : 0, life)
            kinds.push("{k}:{kindOf(r)}")
        },
        @unmount { life.end() },
    )
    effect(@mount {
        var r = slow(100, async.forever)
        key = "b"
    })
}

// The pattern async.query is: a lifetime per mount, ended by the unmount, so
// the request for a key the effect has moved off stops.
func testARekeyCancelsTheOldRequest(t test.Test, c keyed) {
    t.wait(func() => c.kinds.length() == 2, 1500)
    t.assert(c.kinds.contains("a:cancelled") && c.kinds.contains("b:ok"))
}

ui.window {
    manual()
}
